why: Tests step for slice 1 of the mock sweep's lib-top plan (docs/plan/quests/mock-lib-top-PLAN.md at 14e9b3134, decisions 0555 and 0579), in next/. The ten vi.spyOn calls in Id.test.ts and Id.cause.test.ts are gone: nine laws take their random bytes from a SecureRandom made by SecureRandom.make(fill), through generatorWith in Id.test-support.ts, and the allocation-order law checks the exact ids a model of the generator predicts in place of spying on the format check's run. T5 is a type law in Id.types.test.ts. L1 is node's M1: VI_METHODS in oxlint-plugins/builtin-plants.ts and a scenario in oxlint-plugins/plants.test.ts that plants it in every folder of every vitest/no-restricted-vi-methods block. Neither VI_METHODS nor the block existed on origin/main, so this slice created both in node's plan's names and shape (all five methods, fn included, node's messages), with only this plan's two globs in files, so a later fold merges the files lists as a union. On main's Id.ts the nine entropy laws are red because Id.makeGenerator does not exist (Fiber.runLoop: Not a valid effect: undefined), the build's export. Every plant was run against the plan's own sketch of makeGenerator, applied to Id.ts on a saved copy and restored by copy: all thirty Id laws were green on it, and each plant turned its law red. T4's plant (the T518 review 5 P1 shape) turned T4 red, so the plan's doubt about the model law is settled. Under T1's plant the two zero-byte laws first stayed green, since a burst of at most 128 ids never overflows on real random bits; both laws now also check the exact ids of each burst, and turned red under the plant. The plan's claim that the zero laws go red under T1 held only after that addition.
